sn35.83:2.1: Cited at [kv1.6:95.3]() with slight change. | This is the only doctrinal context where we find _vaṭuma_ (“course”). The commentary explains it as the “course of craving”. However, in Buddhist Sanskrit we find the phrases _chinnaṃ vartmaṃ na vartati_ (Mahāvastu 2.416) and _chinnaṃ vartma na pravartate_ (Nidāna Saṁyukta 11.6), which recall the Pali phrase _vaṭṭaṁ vattati_ ([dn15:22.6]()), where _vaṭṭa_ occurs in the next word of the current passage. This suggests that the sense is, rather, the “course of transmigration”, as in the later Sanskrit phrase _saṁsāravartmani_.
